newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich, White House spar over Clinton interview.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich, White House spar over Clinton interview.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich traded partisan potshots with the White House Wednesday over President Clinton's failure to warn against illegal drug use in an interview on the music video cable channel VH-1.

In an open letter to Clinton, a Democrat, the top Republican in Congress lamented the fact that there was no mention of the dangers of drug abuse in the VH-1 special, "Bill Clinton, Rock & Roll President."

"Silence sends a message. And your silence on teen drug use (Tuesday) night sent a powerful unintended message to young people that drug use isn't that big a deal," Gingrich said in his letter, which was faxed to news organisations.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry responded that VH-1's audience is not young people but ageing members of the post Second World War baby boom generation not prone to drug abuse. He speculated that Gingrich's letter "was written by an over-eager staffer" or that the 53-year-old lawmaker "has been watching too much VH-1."
The irrepressible White House spokesman earlier described VH-1's target audience as "loser boomers," which he defined as "people who sit around reliving their youth on TV."
